L226: # apcore-a2a
L227: 
L228: > Build once, invoke by Code or AI. Every call validated, authorized, and evidenced.
L229: 
L230: apcore-a2a is an automatic 【105†A2A (Agent-to-Agent)†google.github.io】 protocol adapter for the 【106†apcore】 ecosystem. It allows you to expose any apcore Module Registry as a fully functional, standards-compliant A2A 1.0 agent with zero manual effort.
L231: It solves a common problem: you've built AI capabilities with apcore modules, but you need them to talk to other AI agents over a standard protocol. apcore-a2a reads your existing module metadata (schemas, descriptions, examples) and exposes them as a standards-compliant A2A server — no hand-written Agent Cards, no JSON-RPC boilerplate, no manual task lifecycle management.
L232: ### 🚀 Official SDKs
L233: 
L234: All three SDKs implement the same A2A 1.0 contract defined in this repository's 【107†specs】.
L235: 
L236:   * Python SDK: 【108†aiperceivable/apcore-a2a-python】
L237:   * TypeScript SDK: 【109†aiperceivable/apcore-a2a-typescript】
L238:   * Rust SDK: 【110†aiperceivable/apcore-a2a-rust】
L239: 
L240: * * *
L241: By reading the existing apcore metadata—including `input_schema`, `output_schema`, descriptions, behavioral annotations (readonly, cacheable, paginated, etc.), and AI metadata conventions (x-preconditions, x-cost-per-call, etc.)—apcore-a2a eliminates the need to hand-write Agent Cards, JSON-RPC endpoints, and task lifecycle logic.
L242: ## Key Features
L243:   * 🚀 One-Call Server: Launch a compliant A2A server using `serve(registry)`.
L244:   * 📇 Auto Agent Card: Generates `/.well-known/agent-card.json` (A2A 1.0; `/.well-known/agent.json` alias for 0.3 clients) automatically from your module metadata.
L245:   * 🛠️ Skill Mapping: Converts apcore modules into A2A Skills, preserving schemas and examples; `metadata["display"]["a2a"]` overrides surface-facing fields (§5.13).

L179: 【86†`ad25a7f`】
L180: Minor release across all three SDKs. Raises the runtime floor to apcore 0.31.0 / apcore-toolkit
L181: 0.12.0 and fixes three cross-language divergences the floor raise would otherwise have
L182: reopened or created — none of them a change to this binding's own wire contract, all of them
L183: found by reviewing what the two upstream releases changed rather than by anything failing first.
L184: ### Fixed
L185:   * Rust: the Agent Card ACL filter stopped agreeing with the real enforcement path for an
L186: anonymous caller. `ApCoreAgentExecutor::acl_context` exists specifically to reproduce, out of
L187: pipeline, what apcore's own `BuiltinContextCreation` does before `BuiltinACLCheck` reads it, so
L188: the Agent Card filter and `Executor::call()` agree about what an anonymous caller can see.
L189: Through apcore 0.30, apcore-rust's own `BuiltinContextCreation` manufactured a synthetic
L190: `Identity{id:"@external", type:"external"}` for a null identity — a Rust-only bug; apcore-python
L191: and apcore-typescript never did this — and `acl_context` mirrored it for the same reason it
L192: mirrors everything else that step does. apcore 0.31.0 fixes apcore-rust to match its siblings
L193: (`PROTOCOL_SPEC` decision D-103: a null `identity` stays null, no synthetic `@external`
L194: principal; `caller_id` alone still defaults to the ACL's own sentinel). Left unmirrored past the
L195: floor raise, `acl_context` would have kept synthesizing an `Identity` the real pipeline no
L196: longer does, so an `identity_types` / `roles` conditional ACL rule would evaluate against a
L197: fabricated principal on the discovery path and against `None` on the call path — silently
L198: reopening the exact divergence this method was written to prevent.
L199:   * Python and TypeScript: `global_deadline` reached apcore through a workaround for a bug in
L200: apcore/apcore-js itself, and apcore 0.31.0 fixes that bug in a way that breaks the workaround.
L201: Both bindings map A2A's `execution_timeout` onto apcore's `global_deadline` so the pipeline can
L202: stop cooperatively between streaming chunks — the same shape as 0.7.0's OpenAPI Backend finding
L203: (`apcore-a2a.openapi.spec`, "The runtime floor" section below): the floor becoming load-bearing
L204: for a code path that has nothing to do with the feature that motivated raising it.
L205:     * Python passed `time.monotonic() + execution_timeout`, deliberately, because
L206: apcore-python's own deadline enforcement compared the value against `time.monotonic()`
L207: instead of the documented `time.time()` contract — a bug this binding worked around rather
L208: than reported. apcore 0.31.0 (D-99) fixes that internal comparison to match its own documented
L209: contract, which flips the failure mode: a monotonic value (~1e5–1e6) now reads as
L210: already-expired against `time.time()` (~1.8e9), so every module call through the executor
L211: would have failed immediately, with the defect latent for as long as the manifest still said
L212: `apcore>=0.30.0`.
L213:     * TypeScript seeded `data[CTX_GLOBAL_DEADLINE]` (ms-since-epoch) because apcore-js's

L177: Creation sequence: 1. Build skills via `_skill_mapper` from all registry modules. 2. Determine capabilities (streaming support, push, history). 3. Build Agent Card via `_agent_card_builder.build(...)`. 4. Create `TaskManager(task_store)`. 5. Create `ExecutionRouter(executor, task_manager, part_converter, error_mapper, execution_timeout)`. 6. Create `StreamingHandler(task_manager, router)`. 7. If `push_notifications`: create `PushNotificationManager(task_store)`. 8.
L178: Build Starlette routes: - `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` → Agent Card (no auth); `GET /.well-known/agent.json` served as a 0.3 compat alias - `POST /` → JSON-RPC dispatch - `GET /health` → health check - `GET /agent/authenticatedExtendedCard` → extended card (if auth) 9. Apply `AuthMiddleware` if auth provided. Exempt: `{"/.well-known/agent-card.json", "/.well-known/agent.json", "/health", "/metrics"}`. 10. Apply CORS middleware if `cors_origins` provided. 11.
